title: An optimized measles virus glycoprotein-pseudotyped lentiviral vector production system to promote efficient transduction of human primary B cells
protocol: Transform different vials of One Shot™ Stbl3™ Chemically Competent E. coli cells with 10 ng of pCG-HΔ24, pCG-FΔ30, pMDLg/RRE, pRSV-Rev, and p-MND-eGFP-eCD4-Ig according to the manufacturer’s protocol.
Incubate plates at 37°C overnight for colony formation.
Pick a single colony from each transformation plate after 16 hours.
Inoculate picked colonies into 250 mL ampLB medium in a 1 L flask.
Cover the top of the flask with foil and create small holes with a pipet tip.
Incubate the flask at 37°C with constant shaking (300 rpm) for 16 h overnight.
Create holes on the surface of each flask and use 1L flasks (four times the volume of the culture) to maintain LB saturated with oxygen.
Incubate the cultures for 16 hours.
Collect the culture and load it into a centrifuge tube.
Spin at 4,000×g for 30 minutes at 4°C.
Resuspend the bacterial pellet in 12 mL of Resuspension Buffer RES+RNase A by pipetting up and down and vortexing to ensure homogeneity.
Add 12 mL of lysis buffer LYS to the bacterial lysate, ensuring no precipitation occurs, then gently invert the tube 5 times.
Incubate at room temperature (22°C–24°C) for 5 minutes.
Apply 12 mL of equilibration buffer EQU onto the rim of the NucleoBond® Xtra Column Filter.
Neutralize the lysis buffer by adding 12 mL of buffer NEU and mix thoroughly until the lysate is colorless.
Load the lysate on the NucleoBond® Xtra Column Filter.
Add 10 mL of Wash Buffer EQU.
Discard the Column Filter after washing with 12 mL of EQU buffer.
Place the column in a sterile 50 mL falcon tube.
Elute plasmid DNA with 5 mL of pre-warmed Elution buffer ELU.
Precipitate eluted plasmid DNA with 3.5 mL of isopropanol and mix thoroughly.
Centrifuge at 4,500 × g for 1 h.
Alternatively, add the isopropanol to the elution column to increase yield.
Decant supernatant and add 10 mL of 70% ethanol.
Wash the pellet by resuspending it in 70% ethanol and ultracentrifuge as above.
Remove supernatant and allow the pellet to air dry at RT for 10 min.
Resuspend the pellet in ethanol and run an hour-long precipitation step to increase quality.
Dissolve DNA pellet in 500 μL of sterile water.
Quantify and qualify plasmid DNA with UV spectrometry and evaluate by restriction digests, respectively.
Aliquot plasmid DNA to avoid multiple freeze-thawing cycles and store at -20°C for up to 2 years.
Prepare 10 cm² tissue culture plates with sterile 0.01% poly-L-lysine solution using a laminar flow tissue culture hood.
Aspirate any remaining solution from plates and let them completely dry inside the tissue culture hood.
Seed CD46KO 293T cells without washing off the poly-L-lysine coated plates.
Split and count CD46KO 293T cells 2 hours later using TrypLE dissociating enzyme.
Seed 5 × 10^6 cells per poly-L-lysine coated plate in 10 mL of cDMEM.
Incubate cells for 16 h in a 37°C, humidified 5% CO2 incubator.
Remove cDMEM medium from the CD46KO 293T cell containing plates 16 hours later.
Replace with 10 mL of fresh cDMEM.
Calculate the volume of each plasmid required per transfection reaction per 10 cm² plate of CD46KO 293T cells.
Add the required plasmid DNA mass in a 1.5 ml Eppendorf tube.
Pipette 62 μL of 2.5 M CaCl₂ into the DNA mixture and mix gently.
Add sterile water to reach a total volume of 500 μl.
Vortex mix the contents and briefly spin down the tube.
Transfer 500 μl of 2× Hepes Buffer Solution (pH 7.0) into a 15 ml polystyrene conical tube.
Bubble filtered air through 500 μL of 2× HBS using a 1 mL serological pipette attached to a pipette aid.
Add the CaCl2-DNA solution drop-wise to the 500 μL HBS while introducing turbulence.
Let the mixture sit at room temperature for 30 minutes until a cloudy solution develops due to precipitate formation.
Pipette the prepared DNA/CaPO4 suspension up and down multiple times.
Slowly add 1 mL of the precipitate to each plate containing CD46KO 293T cells.
Rock the plates back and forth to evenly distribute the precipitate.
Incubate cells for 16 hours at 37°C in a humidified 5% CO2 incubator.
Carefully remove all medium/transfectant from the cells after approximately 16 hours.
Add 5 mL of 3% FBS-DMEM to the cells.
Incubate cells for 24 hours.
Collect supernatant from 3 x 10 cm2 plates through a 0.22 μm PES filter.
Transfer 15 mL of purified MV-LV containing supernatant into ultracentrifuge tubes.
Layer the supernatant onto a 5 mL of filter-sterilized 20% (w/v) sucrose/HBSS cushion.
Harvest only once on day 4.
Use low protein binding PES membrane filters for purification/cell debris removal steps.
Centrifuge the collected supernatant at 400 × g for 5 min at 4°C if CD46KO 293T cells detach and are observed in the supernatant to prevent filter clogging.
Place ultracentrifuge tubes into the SW28 Ti rotor, balancing with appropriately weighted tubes using sterile PBS as needed.
Ultracentrifuge at 19,400 rpm using an SW28 Ti rotor or at 67,865 × g for any other rotor for 2 hours and 20 minutes at 4°C.
Take extra care not to dislodge the pellet when removing ultracentrifuge tubes from the rotor.
Proceed directly to step 26.
Incubate plate containing CD46KO 293T cells with TrypLE for 5 min at 37°C.
Collect transfected CD46KO 293T cells by adding 100 μL in 900 μL of PBS and proceed with flow cytometry sample analysis.
Determine plasmid transfection efficiency using either fluorescence microscopy or flow cytometry.
Add 1 mL of TrypLE to the plate containing transfected CD46KO 293T cells.
Incubate for 5 minutes at 37°C after adding TrypLE.
Remove supernatant from ultracentrifuge tubes into a 10% bleach solution.
Invert tubes onto a sterile paper towel inside a tissue culture hood.
Leave inverted tubes for 2 minutes to allow extra supernatant to drip.
Resuspend pellet in 75 μL IMDM to achieve a 150× concentration.
Pipette up and down at least 100 times in IMDM while limiting foaming.
Aliquot vector and label with MV-LV name and date of production.
Store vector aliquots immediately at −80°C.
Count and seed 3 × 10^5 Nalm6 cells per well in a 6-well plate in a final volume of 2 mL cRPMI.
Seed 12 wells of Nalm6 cells including technical duplicates for serial dilutions from 10^-1 to 10^-5 and two mock transduction samples.
Incubate the seeded Nalm6 cells at 37°C with 5% CO2 for approximately 18 hours post seeding.
Thaw viral supernatants.
Create a series of viral supernatant 1/10 serial dilutions from 10^-1 to 10^-5 in a final volume of 600 μL cRPMI.
Replace old medium with 500 μL fresh cRPMI containing 8 μg/mL polybrene.
Add 500 μL of each viral dilution to 500 μL of polybrene-containing cRPMI.
Mix by pipetting.
Return plates to a 37°C, humidified 5% CO2 incubator for 2 hours.
Seed two extra wells as mock transduced controls.
Add 1 mL of cRPMI to the plates after 2 hours.
Return plates to a 37°C, humidified 5% CO2 incubator.
Collect 100 μL of each cell well per condition 48 hours post-transduction.
Mix collected cells with 400 μL of PBS for flow cytometry preparation.
Pipette 5 mL of PBMCs slowly and dropwise in 20 mL PBS.
Centrifuge PBMCs at 400 × g for 5 min at RT.
Aspirate supernatant, resuspend in 20 mL of PBS and spin down as above.
Count cells.
Aspirate supernatant and depending on the number of cells add up to 8.5 mL of EasySep buffer.
Transfer the total volume in a 14 mL polystyrene round bottom tube.
Add 50 μL of enrichment cocktail per mL of sample.
Leave at RT for 10 min.
Vortex magnetic beads for 30 s.
Mix 75 μL of magnetic beads per mL of sample.
Leave at RT for 5 min.
Add up to 5 mL of EasySep buffer.
Transfer tube into a magnet and incubate at RT for 5 min.
Invert the magnet containing the tube and pour the enriched B cell suspension into a new sterile tube.
Count cells and resuspend in B cell expansion media at a seeding density of 1.5 × 10^6 cells/mL in a final volume of 3–5 mL/well for a 6 well plate.
Collect and pool all cells on day 2.
Resuspend collected cells in IMDM at a concentration of 1.5 × 10^6 cells/mL.
Seed activated primary B cells at a density of 3 × 10^5 cells/well of a 96 well clear flat-bottom plate.
Add 20 μL of MV-LV (5.0 × 10^7–1 × 10^8 TU/mL) to each well and create technical triplicates for each transfer vector or experimental condition.
Spinoculate the samples for 30 min at 400 × g at room temperature.
Incubate the plate in a 37°C, humidified 5% CO2 incubator for 6 hours.
Centrifuge the 96 well plate at 400 × g for 5 minutes at room temperature after 6 hours.
Remove 100 μL of media from each well.
Replace removed media with 100 μL of fresh 2× B cell expansion medium to achieve a final volume of 220 μL of 1× B cell expansion medium per well.
Return the plate to a 37°C, humidified 5% CO2 incubator.
Transfer cultures from each well of the 96 well plate to a 48 well flat bottom plate on day 3.
Add 200 μL of 1× B cell expansion medium to each well for a final volume of 420 μL on day 3.
Transfer cultures from each well of the 48 well plate to a 24 well flat bottom plate on day 5.
Add 400 μL of 1× B cell expansion medium to each well for a final volume of 820 μL on day 5.
Count and transfer 2 × 10^5 B cells per condition to a 96 well round bottom plate on day 7.
Add 100 μL of PBS to the 96 well round bottom plate and centrifuge for 5 min at 400 × g on day 7.
Decant the supernatant from the 96 well round bottom plate.
Add 200 μL of PBS to the 96 well round bottom plate and repeat the spin step as above.

Prepare an extracellular staining master mix containing AF350 LIVE/DEAD™ fixable violet dead cell stain at a dilution of 1:1000, Brilliant Violet 605™ anti-human CD19 antibody at a dilution of 1:200, and Brilliant Violet 785™ anti-human CD3 antibody at a dilution of 1:200 in PBS.
Decant the supernatant.
Add 50 μL of extracellular staining master mix.
Pipette up and down multiple times.
Cover the plate and leave it at 4°C for 30 min in the dark.
Once the extracellular staining step is complete, add 200 μL of PBS.
Repeat the spinning step as above.
Decant the supernatant.
Add 100 μL of Cytofix/Cytoperm™ fixation and permeabilization solution.
Cover the plate and leave it at RT for 20 min in the dark.
Thoroughly mix the cells in the Cytofix/Cytoperm™ solution using gentle pipetting for efficient intracellular staining.
Do not exceed incubation time for more than 20 min.
Add 200 μL of Perm/Wash™ Buffer and spin as above.
Decant the supernatant.
Repeat step from adding Perm/Wash™ Buffer.
Decant the supernatant.
Add 100 μL of Cytoperm™ Permeabilization Buffer Plus.
Cover the plate and leave it at 4°C for 10 min in the dark.
Add 200 μL of Perm/Wash™ Buffer and spin as above.
Decant the supernatant.
Repeat step from adding Perm/Wash™ Buffer.
Decant the supernatant.
Add 100 μL of Cytofix/Cytoperm™ Fixation and permeabilization solution.
Cover the plate and leave it at RT for 5 min in the dark.
Add 200 μL of Perm/Wash™ Buffer and spin as above.
Decant supernatant and repeat the previous step.
Meanwhile, prepare intracellular staining master mix containing PE/Cyanine7 anti-human IgM antibody (dilution 1:200) in Perm/Wash™.
Add 50 μL of the intracellular staining master mix to the cells.
Pipette up and down multiple times.
Cover the plate and leave it at 4°C for 30 minutes in the dark.
Prepare compensation beads by mixing 3 drops of positive beads with 3 drops of negative beads and 1 μL of each antibody used in respective tubes.
Mix well and place the rack at 4°C for 30 minutes in the dark.
Add 200 μL of Perm/Wash™ to the cells after intracellular staining is complete.
Repeat spinning step as above.
Decant supernatant and repeat the previous step.
Resuspend pelleted stained cells in 250 μL PBS.
Exclude doublets and dead cells by FSC, SSC, and AF350 LIVE/DEADTM fixable violet dead cell stain.
Select the CD3- population to exclude T cells.
Assess transduction efficiency by measuring the eGFP+ population.
Perform B cell phenotypic analysis with CD19 marker staining.
Assess immunoglobulin expression with IgM staining.
Collect activated human primary B cells.
Centrifuge collected B cells for 5 minutes at 300 × g at room temperature.
Resuspend pellet in 200 μL of PBS.
Proceed to gDNA extraction using the DNeasy Blood and Tissue kit (Qiagen).
Add 20 μL proteinase K and 200 μL of Buffer AL.
Mix thoroughly by vortexing.
Incubate samples at 56°C for 10 minutes for efficient cell lysis.
Add 200 μL pure ethanol to the sample.
Mix the sample thoroughly by vortexing.
Pipette the sample into a DNeasy Mini spin column placed in a 2 mL collection tube.
Centrifuge at ≥6,000 × g for 1 minute at room temperature.
Discard the flow-through and return the spin column to the same collection tube.
Add 500 μL of Buffer AW1 in the spin column.
Centrifuge as above.
Add 500 μL Buffer AW2 in the spin column.
Centrifuge for 3 minutes at 20,000 × g at room temperature.
Discard the collection tube.
Transfer the spin column to a new 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube.
Add 50 μL of water to the center of the spin column membrane.
Incubate for 5 min at room temperature.
Centrifuge for 1 min at ≥ 6,000 × g at room temperature.
Proceed to nanodrop after ensuring a distinct 260 nm peak of ≥10 ng/mL gDNA.
Dilute primers and probes at 100 μM.
Prepare a 20× concentration stock for primers and probes by mixing 59 μL of water with 5 μL of probe, 18 μL of forward primer, and 18 μL reverse primer for each target.
Add 25 ng of extracted genomic DNA to a 25 μL PCR reaction mix containing 2× ddPCR Supermix for probes.
Include a 20× primer/probe set (p+p) for the HIV-1 target sequences and a 20× p+p set for MKL2 reference gene in the PCR reaction mix.
Place an 8 channel disposable droplet generator cartridge into a cartridge holder.
Add 20 μL of the reaction sample into each cartridge well.
Load 70 μL of droplet generation oil into each sample.
Attach the gasket to the cartridge holder and place the set in the droplet generator.
Repeat per sample to create technical duplicates.
Always load the sample first followed by addition of the droplet generation oil to prevent blockage of the cartridge channel microfluidics.
Remove the cartridge holder from the droplet generator and discard the gasket.
Carefully transfer 40 μL of each droplet emulsion to a 96-well propylene plate using a multichannel pipette.
Heat-seal the plate with foil using the PX1 PCR plate sealer.
Place the sealed plate in a Bio-Rad T100 Thermal Cycler.
Transfer the 96-well plate to a QX100 Droplet Reader for data acquisition.
Load Quantasoft software and click ‘Setup’.
Select ‘VCN’ as the type of experiment.
Assign HIV-1-FAM as Channel 1-Unknown.
Assign MKL2-HEX as Channel 2-Reference.
Save your experimental set up.
Press ‘Run’ to start the data acquisition process.
Wait for the droplet reading to complete, indicated by all four indicator lights turning green.
Open the door and remove the plate holder from the unit.
Click ‘Analyze’ to proceed to data analysis.
Set the gates (in 1D Amplitude) by identifying the negative and positive fluorescence signals in the positive control sample reactions.
Export your data.
